threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newcomer by how they still say 'the Tube' instead of just 'the Overground'—classic sign they haven’t quite settled in yet.
Last night on the 59, a guy with two parrots kept insisting they could beatbox—wasn’t half bad, honestly. Brixton never gets dull.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy in a suit discussing poetry with a vendor selling döner at midnight. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find entire streets lined with pop-up Biergärten, where locals set up picnic tables right next to the U-Bahn tracks.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local knows to avoid 16th St BART on a game day; it's like a human tide of jerseys and lost tourists clamoring for directions.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus stuck behind a street performer doing the worm. The crowd cheered, but no one seemed in a hurry to get on board.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about trendy bars, but they miss the everyday scenes at the tiny bakeries where locals queue for fresh pa de xapata.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still taking photos of the metro maps on their phones, trying to figure out the blue line. Everyone else just knows it’s always delayed.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions at the bus stop instead of checking your phone like everyone else. Makes you stand out in an area that's all about the apps.
Last night on the 333, a guy was arguing with the driver about the time, saying he'd never catch the last tube. Classic Brixton desperation.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a full suit casually getting a döner at 3 AM while chatting with a street musician. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find street vendors offering vegan currywurst at 2 AM, right next to techno clubs. The blend of flavors and beats is unmatched.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they dodge the pigeon poop like it’s an Olympic sport and know the exact time the taco truck rolls in.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Had to duck under a Muni bus while waiting for the 5. Didn't even flinch. Just another Wednesday in the Tenderloin, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about Gaudí; they miss the quiet corners where locals sip vermut, sharing stories older than the Sagrada Família.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their tendency to double-check metro maps at every station instead of just blending into the flow of locals.
